topic: Exact quotient and nuisance-minimax inference for off-target exposure levels in discrete IV models. Let finite randomized Z have m arms, binary Y, and X=T union C. Require well-defined Z-excluded Y_t only for t in T; allow unrestricted X(z), and fully saturated arm-specific responses R_{c,z} for c in C. Prove that the sharp identified set for law(Y_T) depends only on skeleton cells p(X=t,Y=y|Z=z), equals the image of the reduced type simplex (T union {star})^Z times {0,1}^T, and is independent of |C| by an explicit right inverse. Conditional on arm counts, factor the full experiment into skeleton counts and a variation-independent nuisance allocation; for every convex loss prove the precise nuisance-minimax reduction R_q(delta0)<=sup_eta R_(q,eta)(delta), not pointwise domination. Adapt Song et al.'s method-of-types KL region for simultaneous finite-sample coverage of the entire reduced identified set, including endpoint kinks; state calibration and computation as independent of |C| but exponential in m and |T|, and prove feasible-law Hoffman/dual excess-width bounds plus a regular-face n^-1/2 lower bound. Verify by exact enumeration the Z={0,1},T={a,b},C={c} witness with z0 masses (a,0)=1/2,(c,1)=1/2 and z1 masses (a,0)=1/2,(c,0)=1/2: saturated responses give E[Y_b-Y_a] bounds [-1/2,1], while a common excluded Y_c gives [0,1]. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: represent reduced atoms r by x_z in T union {star} and y_T; the incidence map A records target cells and star mass and B records law(Y_T). Refine each star coordinate independently using eta_z(c,y)=p(c,y|z)/s(z,star), with a boundary convention at zero star mass, to obtain a full-law right inverse. Conditional multinomial likelihood then splits into a (2|T|+1)-cell skeleton factor and an eta_z allocation factor. For d=2|T|+1 use rho_z=[log(m/alpha)+(d-1)log(n_z+1)]/n_z in D(hat s_z||s_z), followed by reduced-polytope projection. Credit Gabriel et al. for finite coarsening cases, Song et al. for categorical-IV KL projection, Boushehrian et al. for exponential target-dimension limits, Sachs et al. for response LPs, and Levis et al. for active-facet inference. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: prove the simplex/equality-system Hoffman statement for scalar support functions and keep every novelty claim confined to target-specific exclusion quotienting, nuisance-minimax equivalence, arbitrary finite cardinalities, and |C|-free inference. EARLY KILL TEST: enumerate the 36 reduced columns and corresponding 144 saturated full types for m=2,|T|=2, compare random support functions across multiple |C|, and require the displayed bounds exactly.

open_problems.open_problem: For arbitrary finite instrument support and target set T, does target-only outcome exclusion imply that the sharp identified set for law(Y_T) is exactly the image of the reduced response-type simplex (T union {star})^Z times {0,1}^T and is invariant to the number and labels of off-target exposure levels?

source_refs.claim: Two- and three-level calculations show that bounds for effects between well-defined exposure levels can survive coarsening or contamination of off-target levels; arbitrary finite support is not characterized.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, Arvid Sjölander

source_refs.claim: The fully excluded categorical-IV model characterizes compatible joint potential-outcome laws but defines potential outcomes for every exposure category.
source_refs.author: Yilin Song, F. Richard Guo, K. C. Gary Chan, Thomas S. Richardson

source_refs.claim: Response-function variables translate broad classes of discrete causal models and linear causal queries into LPs with tight bounds.
source_refs.author: Michael C. Sachs, Gustav Jonzon, Arvid Sjölander, Erin E. Gabriel
source_refs.venue: Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics

open_problems.why_unsolved: Gabriel et al. establish the off-target invariance pattern only in low-cardinality coarsening cases, whereas Song et al. characterize a different model that imposes exclusion for every treatment category. Searches for target-specific exclusion, off-target exposure quotients, and categorical-IV quotienting found no arbitrary-cardinality theorem. The missing proof is a surjectivity argument: after collapsing every off-target realized exposure to star, each star coordinate must be refined into arbitrary arm-specific (c,y) allocations while preserving the reduced target-potential-outcome law, including zero-star-mass boundary cases.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An equality-of-images theorem for B({r>=0: Ar=s}), together with an explicit right inverse from every reduced law to a saturated full response law for all finite m, T, and C.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation separates scientifically meaningful exposure levels from ill-defined or contaminated levels and asks which valid IV bounds survive that distinction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Scientific interest concerns selected levels of a finer exposure -> interventions on other coarsened levels may be ill-defined -> low-cardinality calculations show invariance -> determine the exact arbitrary-cardinality quotient for target potential outcomes

method_exemplars.technique: Encode deterministic response functions as simplex columns, derive observable incidence equations and the target map, and prove sharpness by constructing a compatible response-function distribution.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The reduced set is the image of a response-type simplex under incidence and target maps; the new step is quotienting full columns and constructing a right inverse.

method_exemplars.technique: Project a multinomial KL confidence region through categorical-IV compatibility constraints to obtain confidence regions for convex counterfactual functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the reduced image theorem is available, the same projection architecture can estimate the target-law set without retaining off-target categories.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a method-of-types KL region on the reduced (2|T|+1)-cell armwise skeleton be projected to give simultaneous finite-sample coverage of the entire sharp law(Y_T) identified set, uniformly through endpoint kinks and with calibration independent of |C|?

source_refs.claim: The categorical-IV paper projects a KL-based multinomial confidence region to obtain confidence regions for convex functions of the joint counterfactual law.
source_refs.author: Yilin Song, F. Richard Guo, K. C. Gary Chan, Thomas S. Richardson

source_refs.claim: A uniform Chernoff-type tail bound is proved for multinomial empirical KL divergence, improving the classical method-of-types bound.
source_refs.author: F. Richard Guo, Thomas S. Richardson

source_refs.claim: Balke-Pearl endpoint functionals are nonsmooth; root-n inference uses a margin condition, while smoothing gives conservative bounds.
source_refs.author: Alexander W. Levis, Matteo Bonvini, Zhenghao Zeng, Luke Keele, Edward H. Kennedy
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: Song et al.'s full categorical construction calibrates on all observed categories and therefore inherits dependence on total exposure cardinality, while Levis et al. show why plug-in or Wald arguments become nonregular at facet switches. The unfilled step is to establish the target-only quotient before concentration, apply the armwise multinomial KL bound at dimension d=2|T|+1, union-calibrate over m arms, and prove that projection covers the whole set rather than a selected endpoint.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A nonasymptotic theorem that projecting the armwise region D(hat s_z||s_z)<=[log(m/alpha)+(d-1)log(n_z+1)]/n_z through the reduced response polytope covers the complete law(Y_T) identified set with probability at least 1-alpha, including laws on kinked faces.

writing_exemplar.why: It integrates categorical-IV characterization, finite-sample KL calibration, and projection into one identification-to-inference narrative.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Categorical IV models produce set-valued conclusions -> multinomial sampling error must propagate through compatibility constraints -> KL regions provide finite-sample protection -> reduce the observable alphabet before projection for |C|-free simultaneous coverage

method_exemplars.technique: Bound the moment-generating function of nD(hat p||p) uniformly over multinomial p and invert the resulting Chernoff tail bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each randomized arm supplies one reduced multinomial vector, so the inequality can be union-calibrated and projected.

method_exemplars.technique: Build the response-function incidence matrix and optimize linear causal queries over its feasible simplex.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Projection of each accepted skeleton law requires this response-type LP representation of the target set.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze maxima and minima of competing bound formulas through active indices, margin conditions, influence functions, and smooth approximations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It isolates the endpoint-kink phenomenon that finite-sample set projection must cover without assuming a stable active facet.

open_problems.open_problem: Conditional on randomized-arm counts, can the full categorical-IV experiment be factored into reduced skeleton counts and a variation-independent off-target allocation nuisance so that every full-data rule under convex loss has a skeleton-based rule satisfying the sharp nuisance-minimax risk reduction, without claiming pointwise domination?

source_refs.claim: Blackwell characterizes comparison of statistical experiments through attainable risks and randomization kernels, providing the decision-theoretic template for information reduction.
source_refs.author: David Blackwell

source_refs.claim: Off-target ill-defined or contaminated exposure levels can be irrelevant for low-cardinality target-effect bounds even though their observed cells remain in the data.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, Arvid Sjölander

source_refs.claim: Categorical-IV inference is formulated from the full multinomial observed law and therefore retains every treatment-outcome cell.
source_refs.author: Yilin Song, F. Richard Guo, K. C. Gary Chan, Thomas S. Richardson

open_problems.why_unsolved: This is a technique-derived application of comparison-of-experiments logic to a partially identified causal target. The skeleton is not sufficient for the full parameter because conditional off-target labels depend on eta, so ordinary Rao-Blackwell conditioning cannot yield a parameter-free rule or pointwise risk improvement. The first changed proof step is to exploit the product multinomial factorization and take a supremum over the variation-independent eta before applying convexity. Searches combining categorical IV, skeleton counts, nuisance minimax, and experiment comparison found no occupied target-method pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample factorization theorem and explicit randomized reduction from delta to delta0 proving R_q(delta0)<=sup_eta R_(q,eta)(delta) for every convex loss, with a converse or equality characterization when attainable.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives the clearest causal motivation for treating observed off-target categories as potentially irrelevant to target contrasts.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Only selected exposure interventions are meaningful -> off-target cells remain observable but need not obey exclusion -> identification suggests those cells contain nuisance detail -> ask whether the statistical experiment admits the same target-nuisance separation

method_exemplars.technique: Construct Markov randomizations between experiments and compare their attainable risk sets over decision problems.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result compares full and skeleton multinomial experiments, but only after adversarial optimization over the allocation nuisance.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit exact multinomial likelihood structure and relative-entropy concentration uniformly over categorical probability vectors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The skeleton-allocation decomposition is a multinomial factorization and must remain valid at zero cells where nuisance allocations need a boundary convention.

open_problems.open_problem: For the reduced response-type equality system Ar=s, can one obtain computable global Hoffman or dual constants that bound feasible-set excess and every scalar support-function perturbation while remaining independent of off-target cardinality?

source_refs.claim: Hoffman's theorem bounds distance to the solution set of a consistent linear inequality system by a constant times the constraint residual.
source_refs.author: Alan J. Hoffman
source_refs.venue: Journal of Research of the National Bureau of Standards

source_refs.claim: Sharp Lipschitz constants for feasible and optimal LP solution sets under right-hand-side perturbations are expressed through pseudoinverses of constraint submatrices.
source_refs.author: Wu Li

source_refs.claim: Support functions turn estimation of compact convex identified sets into value-function inference, but do not provide an IV-incidence-specific global perturbation modulus.
source_refs.author: Hiroaki Kaido

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic Hoffman theory controls distance to a polyhedron, and generic partial-identification theory treats support-function inference, but the bridge is not automatic for a probability simplex intersected with equalities when the observable right-hand side approaches its boundary. The first proof step is an equality-plus-nonnegativity Hoffman bound restricted to the simplex, followed by passage through the target map B and LP duality to a uniform scalar support bound. Searches found no IV response-simplex-specific modulus, much less one invariant to off-target refinement.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving excess(BF(s'),BF(s))<=K_AB||s'-s|| and |h_BF(s')(u)-h_BF(s)(u)|<=K_AB||u||_*||s'-s|| for feasible skeleton laws, with a dual formula or computable upper bound for K_AB independent of |C|.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates support functions as the operational language for inference on compact convex identified sets and links them to optimization value functions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Partial identification produces a compact convex set -> support functions encode its boundary and scalar queries -> sampling perturbs the defining constraints -> obtain an IV-specific deterministic modulus converting skeleton error into set and endpoint error

method_exemplars.technique: Convert linear-constraint residual size into distance from an approximate point to the exact feasible polyhedron.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The reduced response-law fiber is defined solely by linear incidence equalities, simplex normalization, and nonnegativity.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive right-hand-side Lipschitz constants for LP feasible and optimal solution mappings from pseudoinverses of active constraint submatrices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Skeleton sampling error perturbs only the right-hand side Ar=s, exactly the perturbation regime analyzed by Li.

method_exemplars.technique: Use LP duality to represent support functions as value functions and normalize their sampling fluctuations for inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After the Hoffman step controls feasible fibers, the desired excess-width statement concerns the same dual support values used for set inference.

open_problems.open_problem: What are the sharp minimax rates for estimating support endpoints of the reduced target-specific IV identified set across regular faces and facet kinks, uniformly over arbitrary off-target cardinality?

source_refs.claim: The analysis obtains root-n behavior under a margin condition and conservative smoothing for nonsmooth causal-bound functionals, without a complete minimax rate characterization.
source_refs.author: Alexander W. Levis, Matteo Bonvini, Zhenghao Zeng, Luke Keele, Edward H. Kennedy
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: Regularized support-function estimators yield uniform Gaussian limits for polygonal identified sets with flat faces and remain sharp-set consistent in nonregular cases.
source_refs.author: Bulat Gafarov

source_refs.claim: A dual relationship between level-set estimators and support functions yields Wald-type inference for compact convex identified sets.
source_refs.author: Hiroaki Kaido

open_problems.why_unsolved: Levis et al. give root-n upper results under separation and conservative smoothing without a complete minimax phase diagram, while Gafarov regularizes polygonal support functions under affine moment restrictions. Neither analysis exploits an exact causal quotient removing arbitrarily many nuisance categories. The local experiment changes when multiple dual optima meet at a facet kink: a regular-face LAN lower bound requires a nonzero derivative of the reduced support value, while uniform rates require controlling near-ties among reduced LP dual solutions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax theorem over stated margin classes giving matching n^-1/2 lower and upper rates on regular faces, the correct slower or non-Gaussian rate at kinks, and an attaining estimator whose constants and calibration do not depend on |C|.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames causal-bound endpoints as nonsmooth statistical functionals and separates direct from smoothed estimation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: IV assumptions identify bounds rather than an ATE -> endpoint formulas are maxima or minima and hence nonsmooth -> margin conditions recover root-n behavior but do not settle optimality -> determine the minimax regular-face and kink phase diagram

method_exemplars.technique: Use active-bound indices, margin exponents, influence-function corrections, and local perturbations to control endpoint-estimation bias.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Reduced IV endpoints are maxima or minima of finitely many dual linear forms, with the same active-face nonregularity.

method_exemplars.technique: Regularize a polyhedral support value, prove a uniform Gaussian approximation, and remove first-order regularization bias.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination estimand is a support endpoint of a finite polytope whose optimizer may switch or be nonunique.

method_exemplars.technique: Express identified-set inference through the dual support-function value and derive normalized Wald statistics.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The reduced target set is compact and convex, so its scalar endpoints and directional laws are naturally represented by support functions.

literature_map:
1. Manski (1990, AER Papers and Proceedings) established assumption-lean sharp treatment-effect bounds and the partial-identification viewpoint.
2. Balke and Pearl (1997, JASA, doi:10.1080/01621459.1997.10474074) derived tight binary-IV ATE formulas through latent response types and linear programming.
3. Bonet (2001, UAI, arXiv:1301.2258) showed that discrete IV models have nontrivial observable instrumentality constraints.
4. Richardson and Robins (2014/2024, arXiv:1410.0470 and arXiv:2401.13758) treated binary exposure and outcome with an instrument of arbitrary finite support.
5. Sachs et al. (2023, JCGS, arXiv:2003.10702) automated response-function LP construction and sharp symbolic bounds for broad discrete causal models.
6. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjölander (2025, Biostatistics, arXiv:2401.17735) distinguished meaningful target levels from ill-defined or contaminated off-target levels and derived low-cardinality bounds.
7. The arbitrary-cardinality boundary remains: the observed invariance pattern has not been proved for general finite target and off-target alphabets.
8. Song et al. (2024, arXiv:2405.09510) characterized the fully excluded categorical-IV model and projected multinomial KL regions to counterfactual-law functionals.
9. Guo and Richardson (2021, IEEE TIT, arXiv:2003.08614) supplied the uniform empirical-KL concentration inequality behind that finite-sample construction.
10. Levis et al. (2025, JRSSB, arXiv:2301.12106) showed that IV bound endpoints are nonsmooth active-facet functionals and used margin conditions or smoothing for inference.
11. Blackwell (1953, Annals of Mathematical Statistics) supplies experiment-comparison machinery, but no located work applies it to target-only categorical-IV nuisance allocations.
12. Hoffman (1952) and Li (1993, LAA) provide residual-to-feasible-set and LP perturbation constants; Kaido (2016, Journal of Econometrics) connects dual support values to identified-set inference.
13. Gafarov (2025, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1904.00111) regularizes polygonal support functions for uniform inference at flat faces.
14. Boushehrian et al. (2026, arXiv:2604.12802) prove exponential lower bounds for sharp analytical discrete-IV descriptions, leaving post-quotient complexity in m and |T| unresolved.
15. Targeted searches found no arbitrary-cardinality target-specific-exclusion quotient, |C|-free simultaneous finite-sample region, nuisance-minimax skeleton theorem, or IV-specific Hoffman modulus.
